subject: TrustBound connectivity: peering vs PrivateLink vs site-to-site VPN
messages:
From: Rajesh Menon <r.menon@trustbound.io>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: networking@trustbound.io
Date: Tue, 2 May 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: TrustBound POC - connectivity options and what we need

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are ready to start a short POC (2-3 weeks) to validate Redwood Private against our on-prem LLM inference needs. Before we kick off the lab, our security and network teams asked for a recommendation on connectivity approaches. The three options they want scoped: VPC Peering (direct peering to Redwood-managed VPC), PrivateLink (interface endpoints / AWS PrivateLink to Redwood service endpoints), or classic site-to-site VPN (IPsec tunnel into Redwood edge).

Quick context on our constraints:
- We cannot accept inbound public IPs to our on-prem systems.
- Source IP visibility matters for our audit logs (we prefer that back-end sees originating customer IPs when possible).
- Some of our downstream services are NATed behind an appliance; we can punch dedicated NAT rules if required.
- Cost sensitivity for POC (short-lived), but long-term SLA and maintainability are higher priority.

Attached: TrustBound-network-map-v1.pdf and an access requirements spreadsheet. Can you and your network SME lay out pros/cons from Redwood's perspective and call out the operational checklist for each path (routing, NAT, firewall rules, mutual-auth, failover)?

Can we aim for a short write-up by EOD tomorrow and a quick alignment call Thursday?

Thanks,
Rajesh
Network Architecture Lead
TrustBound

---

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Rajesh Menon <r.menon@trustbound.io>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 2 May 2028 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TrustBound POC - connectivity options and what we need

Rajesh —

Appreciate the clear constraints and the diagrams. Looping in Kimberly (Private deployments) and Marcus (Networking/runtime) — they will sketch tradeoffs and checklist items. We can deliver a short decision memo by EOD Wed and propose a 30m alignment call Thu 10am PT.

High-level previews from my side:
- VPC Peering: simplest from a connectivity point-of-view for low latency and preserving source IPs, but it requires us to coordinate CIDR allocations and cross-account peering ACLs. No support for transitive routing; works great if TrustBound wants dedicated private connectivity without an endpoint abstraction.
- PrivateLink: gives endpoint-level connectivity (interface ENIs) and avoids exposing a full CIDR, good for multi-tenant isolation and customer-managed VPCs. It hides backend instance IPs (Redwood terminates the endpoint), which may complicate your source-IP audit requirement unless we preserve X-Forwarded-For or pass along a proxied header (requires NLB + proxy shim). More operational glue for certs and endpoint management.
- Site-to-site VPN: lowest initial procurement friction (we can spin up an IPsec tunnel), flexible for on-prem NATed environments, but adds latency and jitter; IP visibility depends on NAT and the tunnel termination point. Also requires monitoring and BGP if you want dynamic routing/redundancy.

We'll attach explicit firewall rule snippets and a small runbook per approach.

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Rajesh Menon <r.menon@trustbound.io>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 May 2028 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TrustBound POC - connectivity options and what we need

Rajesh —

Attached is the brief memo you asked for (see inline below + attachments). Summary and recommendation up front:

Recommendation: Start POC with a short-lived site-to-site IPsec tunnel for speed of onboarding and then graduate to either VPC Peering (if you want source-IP fidelity and stable CIDR mapping) or PrivateLink (if you want endpoint isolation and reduced blast radius) for production.

Reasoning:
- Site-to-site VPN: fast to stand up, minimal changes on your edge appliance. Good for POC because we can iterate network rules quickly. Drawbacks: higher jitter/latency and maintenance overhead; for production, we'd prefer a managed peering or PrivateLink.
- VPC Peering: preserves packet-level source IPs (no NAT required at tunnel), lowest steady-state latency, but requires CIDR planning and peering approvals; also requires us to coordinate cross-account route-table and potentially inter-region considerations. Not ideal if you need many small customer VPCs (scale cost/ops).
- PrivateLink: best security posture for multi-tenant hosted control plane; however, it terminates at an interface endpoint and commonly requires a proxy to preserve origin IPs in the application layer (XFF header) — we'll provide a proxy pattern for log preservation. It also simplifies firewall rules on your side — allow only the endpoint ENI IPs.

Operational checklist (high level):
- VPN POC: Create IPsec S2S tunnel (Redwood edge IPs to your edge appliance), configure static routes or BGP, open UDP 500/4500 and ESP on both sides, and add route exceptions for the LLM endpoint subnets. Run perf tests (p50/p95 RTT) and packet loss checks.
- VPC Peering: Exchange VPC IDs and CIDR ranges; request cross-account peering; update route tables and security groups; ensure no overlapping CIDRs; validate metrics for egress accounting.
- PrivateLink: Request creation of interface endpoint service; provide the service name and required security groups; configure TLS certs and service principals; deploy lightweight proxy (NLB -> proxy -> application) if you need real client IPs in logs.

What we need from TrustBound for the POC:
1) Preferred IP ranges we can peer (if choosing peering) or edge appliance public IP for VPN termination.
2) A list of audit/inventory points where source IPs must appear (so we can tailor proxy headers).
3) Proof-of-access window this week (Thu 10am PT works for us) for a 30-minute alignment call to agree on the POC transport.

I've attached a simple runbook and firewall snippets (trustbound-access-requirements.xlsx). If you want, Marcus can drop a short network diagram that overlays how X-Forwarded-For will be preserved for PrivateLink.

Next steps: Confirm preferred POC path and provide the edge IP / CIDR by Wed EOD; we'll provision the corresponding artifacts and send connection instructions before Thu call.

Kimberly Park
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference

Thanks Kimberly/Tessa — this is really helpful.

Decision: For the POC we'll stand up an IPsec tunnel first (fastest). Our security team still wants to see the PrivateLink pattern for production because it limits blast radius, but they have a hard requirement that our SIEM must see original client IPs in logs for compliance.

Action items from TrustBound:
- We'll provision the edge public IP and a small /28 for the peering experiment (hold while we test).
- We'll send the list of SIEM endpoints that must receive enriched XFF headers if you use PrivateLink.
- Thu 10am PT works — I'll send a calendar invite.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Rajesh
